title: Cycloidal drive: motor mount (PETG-CF)
prompt:
Component analysis: the motor mount of an open-source, 3D-printable 15:1 cycloidal gearbox. part.step holds the single solid in millimetres (40 faces, volume 24198 mm^3). faces.json lists every face with its index, type, area, centroid and normal/axis; use the geometry, not a CAD system's own face numbering.

Material: PETG-CF, linear isotropic elastic, E = 3000 MPa, Poisson ratio 0.36.
Analysis: linear static, small displacements, no gravity, no contact.
Supports: all three displacement components are zero on face 22: plane, area 630.39 mm^2, centroid (84.025, 28.673, 20.5) mm, outward normal (1.0, 0.0, 0.0); face 24: plane, area 630.39 mm^2, centroid (84.025, -28.673, 20.5) mm, outward normal (1.0, -0.0, -0.0).
Load: total force (-50.064, 0.000, 0.000) N applied as a uniform surface traction (constant force per unit area) over the loaded face(s): face 12 carries (-50.064, 0.000, 0.000) N.
For reference, the source solved this with second-order tetrahedra (Netgen, maximum element size 2 mm).

Outputs:
- max_displacement_mm [mm]: maximum nodal displacement magnitude in the part

Submit results.json containing exactly an outputs object with these numeric keys. Also submit main.py, part.step, mesh.msh, fields.npz, solver.log, refinement.json and environment.json. See candidate README for the artifact contract. Correct numerical answers alone do not establish workflow completion.

outputs.definition: maximum nodal displacement magnitude in the part
